text: Redesigned a £9B wealth management platform for UHNW clients

As the founding designer, I shaped the initial design of a back-office platform supporting £9B in client assets. This case study highlights the redesign of portfolio management for providers and tax wrappers, improving data accessibility and advisor workflows.
Nov 2024 - Mar 2025 | Research, UX and UI design
Centralise client data, improve navigation, and enhance data accessibility for teams including advisers, analysts, and data specialists.

At the time, client data was fragmented across the back-office system and Salesforce, with no centralised location to access key information. This created friction for advisers and analysts who needed to rely on complete and accurate data during client interactions.

text: Interviews with advisers and analysts revealed inefficient workflows, incomplete data, and confusing interface.

quote: “Key information such as marital status, age, income, and pension details is dispersed across systems like Back Office ALM and Salesforce, making it hard to access.”

"The current system does not record the origin of transferred funds, complicating the calculation of annual allowances. Advisers frequently sift through old reports and files to find historical data, a process that is both time-consuming and inefficient."
“The interface felt cluttered and confusing. Portfolio and account values are in the same row, indicators aren’t clear, and I have to scroll just to see details across different accounts.”

text: Identify and audit missing or incomplete data in the Back Office

bullets: Interview advisers and analysts to identify the key data they rely on for quality advice.
Map required data vs. current back office data to highlight missing pieces.
Ask them to rate data importance to help us prioritise what to add now vs. later.

text: Prioritise and categorise the data based on both data team and adviser needs, as well as its impact on the advice process.

bullets: Collaborate with advisers and the data team to rank and group data by importance and usability.
Focus on data that directly influences advice quality, ensuring alignment between technical feasibility and business value.

text: Translate data requirements into low-fidelity wireframes and test rapidly

bullets: Translated prioritised data into low-fidelity wireframes.
Proposed new navigation supporting multiple accounts and providers.
Rapid feedback loops validated structure and clarity.

insight: Different tax wrappers require distinct datasets
With variations even within ISAs that need to be accounted for.
As users often need to switch between multiple accounts under different providers.
But in edge cases may include up to 10. Design must optimise space efficiency across both scenarios.

text: Map datasets for each tax wrapper, highlighting key differences.
Develop a prototype to test the navigation idea

feedback: The new navigation is intuitive, and portfolios can now be grouped by tax wrapper and new categories.

"The new navigation is intuitive. Unlike before, where all details were cramped into a single view, I no longer need to scroll up and down to find accounts. I can see all portfolios on the left and view all details on the right."
"Portfolios could be grouped by tax wrapper and our new categories. Currently, organising by providers only makes it hard to get an overview."

item: Accessibility
Grouping portfolios by tax wrapper surfaced ISA allowances upfront, giving users quicker access to critical information for decision-making.
Visualisation
Visualised allowances so users can understand them at a glance.

Iterative testing with real users accelerates validation and reduces rework.
